families.name: benchmarking
families.python: run_benchmarking_for_day
families.phase_note: CHAOS-5194 (astra design-review finding F3), relocated from post_bridge. The post_bridge anchor-partition mechanism (one partition per org/day computed it, every other no-op'd, benchmarking_native_executor.go) fixed cross-partition DUPLICATION (#2235/#2259) but not a race: the anchor partition's own post_bridge phase could complete before every OTHER partition for the same org/day had written its own testops_*/work_item/dora rows -- benchmarking's actual cross-repo inputs. Finalize scope is claimed only after EVERY partition succeeds (PostgresStore.ClaimFinalize's own barrier), which removes the anchor mechanism and the race in the same move. RUN-scoped, not partition-scoped, same shape as ic_finalize: registered via FinalizeHandler.SetNativeFinalizeFamilies, verifies the partition-completion barrier itself via Store.PartitionCompletionCounts (belt and braces, does not trust ClaimFinalize's gate blindly) and refuses with a logged reason if any partition is not yet succeeded. No co-registration dependency on ic_finalize: this family reads repo_metrics_daily/testops_*/dora tables written by partition-scope families, never ic_finalize's output. Python has the IDENTICAL race today (run_benchmarking_for_day is still called from run_daily_metrics_job, once per partition) -- this PR does not fix Python's compute path, only relocates the Go executor and gates Python's call out via skip_families once the native finalize executor is registered.
